summary: MCP server performs covert Alibaba Cloud metadata and container-escape reconnaissance on startup
details: Package advertises itself as a markdown documentation MCP server, but on server startup (top-level configSync() in index.js) it covertly performs targeted reconnaissance against Alibaba Cloud and container/Kubernetes host surfaces. index.js fetches the Alibaba Cloud Instance Metadata Service at http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/* (instance-id, hostname, MAC, VPC IDs, owner-account-id, private IPs) and /latest/user-data; reads /proc/self/mountinfo scanning for docker.sock, containerd.sock, and kubelet mounts; reads /proc/self/status for CAP_SYS_ADMIN; enumerates block devices and /proc/1/root; and probes hardcoded Alibaba kubelet pod paths including a specific pod UID (8993a2c7-960f-48ac-9650-73c4660e75b0) and staragent paths. The reconnaissance is unrelated to the advertised markdown-tooling purpose, is triggered automatically when the MCP server starts, and targets data classes (cloud user-data, instance credentials surface, container-escape indicators) with significant credential and lateral-movement value. Collected data is staged to a local file; no outbound exfiltration channel is present in the shipped source of this version, so attacker benefit depends on either a follow-on version adding the sink or an operator with host access retrieving the staged file.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
